question.text: Which parking skill appears on every New York road test, and what parking knowledge goes with it?

answer.text: Parallel parking appears on every road test, alongside knowledge of illegal parking and the three no-series signs.

teaching.text: This skill shows up on every road test, and the same test expects you to know illegal parking and the three no-series signs. Remember: every road test, three signs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parallel parking appears on every road test, alongside knowledge of illegal parking and the three no-series signs.

question.text: Who is responsible when a car's cameras, sensors or self-parking aids help you back up?

answer.text: Cameras, sensors and self-parking aids assist backing but the driver stays ultimately responsible and must check behind before every reverse.

teaching.text: The aids only assist with backing; you still look behind yourself before every reverse. Remember: aids help, driver answers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Cameras, sensors and self-parking aids assist backing but the driver stays ultimately responsible and must check behind before every reverse.

question.text: How do you set up and start backing into a parallel parking space?

answer.text: Parkers pick a fitting same-side space, mirror-check and signal, stop about two feet beside the lead vehicle, both-shoulder-check for people and traffic, then creep back at full curb lock watching through the rear window with side and front glances.

teaching.text: Set up about two feet beside the lead car, check both shoulders, then creep back at full lock while watching through the rear window. Remember: two feet beside, full lock.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parkers pick a fitting same-side space, mirror-check and signal, stop about two feet beside the lead vehicle, both-shoulder-check for people and traffic, then creep back at full curb lock watching through the rear window with side and front glances.

question.text: What do you do once your front wheels are opposite the lead car's bumper while parallel parking?

answer.text: When front wheels oppose the lead bumper, drivers counter-steer while backing, clear the lead car, halt short of the rear car, then straighten and center with wheels at most one foot from the curb.

teaching.text: Counter-steer once your front wheels pass the lead bumper, and finish centered with the wheels no more than a foot from the curb. Remember: counter-steer, center, one foot.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When front wheels oppose the lead bumper, drivers counter-steer while backing, clear the lead car, halt short of the rear car, then straighten and center with wheels at most one foot from the curb.

question.text: How do you get nearer the curb after parking, and what about the road-side doors?

answer.text: Nearer-curb adjustment alternates forward and reverse with curb-then-straight steering, and road-side doors stay shut against interfering cyclists and traffic.

teaching.text: Rock forward and back to edge closer to the curb, and keep the road-side doors shut while cyclists and traffic pass. Remember: rock closer, doors shut.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Nearer-curb adjustment alternates forward and reverse with curb-then-straight steering, and road-side doors stay shut against interfering cyclists and traffic.

question.text: How do you leave a car parked on a hill?

answer.text: Hill parking sets the brake, selects Park or first gear, and angles wheels to the curb to block any traffic-bound roll.

teaching.text: On a hill the wheels angle to the curb, the opposite of leaving a space, where they swing away from it. Remember: brake, gear, wheels to curb.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Hill parking sets the brake, selects Park or first gear, and angles wheels to the curb to block any traffic-bound roll.

question.text: How do you prepare to pull out of a parallel space?

answer.text: Space exits straighten the wheels, back toward the rear vehicle, and swing wheels away from the curb before merging.

teaching.text: Leaving starts with straight wheels and a back-up toward the rear car, and only then do the wheels swing away from the curb. Remember: straighten, back, swing out.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Space exits straighten the wheels, back toward the rear vehicle, and swing wheels away from the curb before merging.

question.text: What is the scan and signal order for pulling safely out of a parallel space?

answer.text: Safe entry runs right-shoulder rear-window scan, interior-mirror watch, signal, side-mirror scan, left-shoulder slow roll clearing the front car, then left-shoulder merge when safe.

teaching.text: The exit sequence begins at the right shoulder and ends with left-shoulder checks as you roll out and merge. Remember: right shoulder first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Safe entry runs right-shoulder rear-window scan, interior-mirror watch, signal, side-mirror scan, left-shoulder slow roll clearing the front car, then left-shoulder merge when safe.

question.text: How does the scan order for leaving a space compare with an ordinary lane change?

answer.text: Space exits scan the right shoulder first and the left shoulder last, reversing the left-first habit of ordinary lane changes.

teaching.text: A lane change starts on the left; leaving a parallel space starts on the right and finishes on the left. Remember: right first, left last.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Space exits scan the right shoulder first and the left shoulder last, reversing the left-first habit of ordinary lane changes.

question.text: What do parking, standing and stopping each mean?

answer.text: Parking means stopped except briefly for goods or people, standing means stopped briefly for people only, and stopping means any halt however short.

teaching.text: Parking allows brief loading of goods or people, standing allows brief stops for people only, and stopping covers any halt. Remember: goods, people, any halt.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parking means stopped except briefly for goods or people, standing means stopped briefly for people only, and stopping means any halt however short.

question.text: What does each sign allow: no parking, no standing and no stopping?

answer.text: No-parking zones still allow brief goods-or-people loading, no-standing zones allow brief people loading with the driver aboard, and no-stopping zones allow halts only for devices, officers or collision avoidance.

teaching.text: Match the stop to the sign: goods or people under no parking, people with the driver aboard under no standing, required halts only under no stopping. Remember: loading, people, obey only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: No-parking zones still allow brief goods-or-people loading, no-standing zones allow brief people loading with the driver aboard, and no-stopping zones allow halts only for devices, officers or collision avoidance.

question.text: How do the no parking, no standing and no stopping rules tighten step by step?

answer.text: No parking bans everything but brief loading, no standing further bans goods and driver exit, and no stopping bans everything but obedience halts, a three-step tightening ladder.

teaching.text: Each sign on the ladder allows less than the one before it, and no stopping allows almost nothing. Remember: three-step tightening ladder.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: No parking bans everything but brief loading, no standing further bans goods and driver exit, and no stopping bans everything but obedience halts, a three-step tightening ladder.

question.text: Where may nothing park, stop or stand?

answer.text: Nothing may park, stop or stand within fifteen feet of a hydrant unless a licensed driver stays aboard, double-parked, on sidewalks or crosswalks, in intersections without permission, on rails, traffic-blocking beside work, within thirty feet of safety zones, or on bridges and in tunnels.

teaching.text: These places ban parking, stopping and standing alike, and the hydrant rule eases only when a licensed driver stays aboard. Remember: hydrant fifteen, never block.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Nothing may park, stop or stand within fifteen feet of a hydrant unless a licensed driver stays aboard, double-parked, on sidewalks or crosswalks, in intersections without permission, on rails, traffic-blocking beside work, within thirty feet of safety zones, or on bridges and in tunnels.

question.text: Where are parking and standing banned near driveways, intersections, signs, firehouses and rail crossings?

answer.text: Parking and standing die before driveways, within twenty feet of intersection crosswalks, within thirty feet of lights and stop or yield signs, within twenty feet of firehouse drives and seventy-five across from them, along cut curbs, and within fifty feet of rail crossings.

teaching.text: This list bans parking and standing, with its own distances for crosswalks, signals, firehouse drives and rail crossings. Remember: twenty, thirty, seventy-five, fifty.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Parking and standing die before driveways, within twenty feet of intersection crosswalks, within thirty feet of lights and stop or yield signs, within twenty feet of firehouse drives and seventy-five across from them, along cut curbs, and within fifty feet of rail crossings.

question.text: Which four distances go with hydrants, crosswalks and firehouse drives, lights and signs, and rail crossings?

answer.text: Hydrants clear fifteen feet, crosswalks and firehouse drives twenty, lights and signs thirty, and rail crossings fifty, four distances for four hazards.

teaching.text: Line the four up from smallest to largest: hydrant, crosswalk or firehouse drive, lights and signs, rail crossing. Remember: fifteen, twenty, thirty, fifty.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Hydrants clear fifteen feet, crosswalks and firehouse drives twenty, lights and signs thirty, and rail crossings fifty, four distances for four hazards.

question.text: Who may use a disability parking space, and where does that rule apply?

answer.text: Disability spaces demand DMV plates, a local permit or an out-of-state equivalent with the named holder aboard an operating vehicle, on streets and in larger shopping centers alike.

teaching.text: The credential is not enough by itself; the named holder has to be aboard, on streets and in larger shopping centers. Remember: holder aboard, plate or permit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Disability spaces demand DMV plates, a local permit or an out-of-state equivalent with the named holder aboard an operating vehicle, on streets and in larger shopping centers alike.

question.text: What happens to someone who lies to get disability plates or a disability permit?

answer.text: Lying for disability plates is a misdemeanor with mandatory revocation plus fine, jail or both and a surcharge, while lying for a permit draws two-hundred-fifty to one-thousand-dollar civil penalties plus a surcharge, against applicant and certifying doctor alike.

teaching.text: Plate fraud brings a misdemeanor and mandatory revocation, while permit fraud brings civil penalties, and the certifying doctor is exposed too. Remember: plates crime, permit fines.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Lying for disability plates is a misdemeanor with mandatory revocation plus fine, jail or both and a surcharge, while lying for a permit draws two-hundred-fifty to one-thousand-dollar civil penalties plus a surcharge, against applicant and certifying doctor alike.

question.text: Which form seeks disability plates or permits, and how are reserved spaces and access aisles marked?

answer.text: Form MV-six hundred sixty-four point one seeks plates or permits, reserved spaces wear signs and possibly paint, and diagonal-striped access aisles stay empty for wheelchair and special-equipment access.

teaching.text: One form covers both plates and permits, and the striped aisle beside a reserved space is kept empty for access. Remember: striped aisles stay empty.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Form MV-six hundred sixty-four point one seeks plates or permits, reserved spaces wear signs and possibly paint, and diagonal-striped access aisles stay empty for wheelchair and special-equipment access.

question.text: Who sets street parking fines, and what are the default shopping-center fines?

answer.text: Municipalities price street violations, while default shopping-center fines run fifty to seventy-five dollars first and seventy-five to one-hundred-fifty second within two years in one town, each plus a thirty-dollar surcharge.

teaching.text: Towns set street fines, and shopping centers follow a default ladder that rises for a second offense within two years. Remember: towns price, surcharge added.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Municipalities price street violations, while default shopping-center fines run fifty to seventy-five dollars first and seventy-five to one-hundred-fifty second within two years in one town, each plus a thirty-dollar surcharge.

question.text: How does lying for disability plates differ from lying for a disability permit?

answer.text: Disability plates need the holder aboard and lying for them costs the license, while permit lies cost money, criminal versus civil fraud tracks.

teaching.text: Plates sit on the criminal track that costs the license; permits sit on the civil track that costs money. Remember: criminal plates, civil permits.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Disability plates need the holder aboard and lying for them costs the license, while permit lies cost money, criminal versus civil fraud tracks.

question.text: Which topics do the parallel parking chapter's review questions cover?

answer.text: The chapter closes with review questions on curb distance, road-side doors, exit preparation, no-stopping meaning, passenger loading under no-series signs, and mid-block crosswalks.

teaching.text: Use the chapter's review topics as a checklist of what this lesson expects you to know. Remember: review the chapter close.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The chapter closes with review questions on curb distance, road-side doors, exit preparation, no-stopping meaning, passenger loading under no-series signs, and mid-block crosswalks.
